title: Hell! Hell! Hell!
summary: Josh and Chuck open the new year with a loose tour of the concept of Hell. They contrast eternal conscious torment (tied to St. Augustine) with universalism and annihilationism, trace how the afterlife and then Hell developed in Sumerian, Egyptian, early Jewish, Canaanite, Mayan and other traditions, and discuss Sheol, Hades, Tartarus, Gehenna, purgatory, limbo and Buddhist naraka. They cover Plato's Myth of Er, Augustine's influence, and Dante's Inferno with its nine circles, contrapasso and the lines over the gate. Hosts share personal religious upbringing anecdotes, a pop culture aside, and a listener mail from Glenda in Australia.

segments.title: Opening banter and framing the Hell episode
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck greet listeners, talk about holiday breaks and a gift, and introduce the topic of Hell with a disclaimer that they are not biblical scholars.

segments.title: Eternal conscious torment versus universalism and annihilationism
segments.summary: Josh defines eternal conscious torment, attributes it to St. Augustine, and contrasts it with universalism (eventual salvation for all) and annihilationism (the wicked cease to exist). They note evangelical pressure against alternatives.

segments.title: Heaven before Hell and early afterlife beliefs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how a heaven concept appeared first and Hell developed from ideas of symmetry, and how Sumerian and other early afterlife beliefs depended on wealth and family offerings. Josh shares his Baptist upbringing.

segments.title: Early Judaism, Sheol and Ecclesiastes
segments.summary: They describe early Jewish views of the afterlife as a state rather than a fiery place, the injustice that everyone goes to the same fate, and how early Jews contrasted themselves with Canaanite religion and child sacrifice.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break; hosts discuss whether one can convert to Judaism.

segments.title: Tartarus, Hades, Gehenna and the underground afterlife
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish Hades, Sheol, Tartarus and Gehenna, with Gehenna as a real burning trash site near Jerusalem that became a metaphor for judgment. They discuss the Mayan Xibalba and the widespread idea that hell lies underground and heaven above.

segments.title: Purgatory, limbo, Buddhist naraka and temperature in hell
segments.summary: They explain purgatory as a place to work off sins, limbo as an eternal state for those before Christ, and the Buddhist and Hindu naraka with hot and cold hells. They discuss why hell is described in such detail.

segments.title: Pandemic waiting-room aside
segments.summary: A short tangent comparing purgatory to a waiting room leads to a conversation about COVID-19 masks and vaccination.

segments.title: Plato's Myth of Er, Augustine and the origins of eternal damnation
segments.summary: They describe Plato's Republic story of Er and how Plato helped popularize the immortal soul and eternal punishment. Augustine is credited with the idea that his interpretation is the correct one and that dissenters may be coerced. Later visionary accounts by Drythelm and Tundale are mentioned.

segments.title: Dante's Inferno, contrapasso and the nine circles
segments.summary: Dante's Divine Comedy from the early 1300s is credited with popularizing Hell's structure of nine circles. The hosts cover contrapasso (poetic justice), the inscription over the gate, Charon and the river Acheron, and Dante's bias against Florence. They walk through the circles from limbo through fraud and Satan at the center.

segments.title: Pop culture versions of Hell
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck mention Bosch paintings, Clive Barker, Marvel, The Good Place, Joyce Carol Oates's short story Night Side, and Albert Brooks's film Defending Your Life.

segments.title: Listener mail from Glenda
segments.summary: Hosts read an email from Glenda, an eighty-year-old listener in Queensland, Australia, who listens on a mobility scooter, thanks Robert for introducing her to the show, and mentions Albert Brooks and Super Dave Osborne.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh invites listeners to send in stories about turning friends onto the show and signs off.
